correctness.rationale: Independent attachment choices imply P(marked leaf)=(i-1)/(n-1). Conditional future choices avoid exactly one parent, yielding t*_(m+1)=[m/(m-1)]t*_m+1-H_(i-1)/(m-1), with unchanged depth of vertex i. Subtract the unconditional exact t_m=m(H_m-1) and induct to obtain a negative harmonic-tail shift. Multiply by leaf probability, exchange finite sums to obtain -(n-2)/4, and use exact adjacent differences plus harmonic approximations to prove a unique asymptotic peak at i/n=1/e. All boundary cases n=2, i=n, i=2 included. The packaged standard-library verifier checked exact enumeration through n=9 and exact finite identities through n=200; numerical large-n checks are not proof.

value.rationale: Leaf count and total root-to-vertex distance are separate, established descriptors of branching topology and search cost. Their joint dependence is not determined by existing marginal laws. The exact negative covariance and label-resolved harmonic influence explain which arrival ages contribute, with the strongest local contribution sharply at an interior fraction 1/e, whereas recent vertices contribute vanishingly. This provides a motivated global and local structural statement beyond a trivial finite computation.
